## Follow-up work (separate initiatives)

- **Per-component CSS loading.** `globalStyles.ts`'s `.zimm-*` class registry is
  registered as one `theme.styles.global` block and ships on every page regardless of
  which classes a given page's components actually use. If component overrides start
  applying `.zimm-*` classNames directly for the non-interactive cases described above,
  only the classes a page's components actually reference should load, not the whole
  registry. Needs its own investigation, not scoped or estimated yet.
- **`globalStyles.ts` adoption is currently near zero.** Of the classes still defined
  there, none have a real consumer anywhere in the app today except one Storybook demo
  (`spacing.stories.tsx`'s `.zimm-grid` example). They're Handover-ported 1:1 and
  presumably _intended_ to be reused, just not adopted by any component yet — worth
  revisiting once component overrides actually start applying them.

## Path A: Figma

### Step 1: Extract from Figma

Use the Figma MCP to read the target frame(s). For each component or screen:

1. Identify the frame name, node ID, dimensions, and layout structure
2. Map all style values to token names from `02-design/library/common.css` (by matching values). If a value cannot be matched to a token, record it as a raw value and flag it.
3. Document all variants and their differences
4. Extract all text content, typography tokens, and colour tokens used
5. Note all interactive elements (buttons, links, inputs, toggles)
6. Note any visible states
7. **Capture the Figma node ID for every functional element** (each interactive element, state-bearing element, filter, group, and tile). These node IDs are the stable identifiers used by the functional fact table (Step 3) and by downstream delta detection. Use the full node ID as returned by the Figma MCP (e.g. `I378:49176;11913:28894`).

### Step 2: Screenshot the frame

Use the Figma MCP `get_screenshot` tool to capture a rendered screenshot of the frame. This step is mandatory. It is not optional.

Save to: `02-design/specs/[type]/[component-name]/assets/YYYY-MM-DD-screenshot.png` using today's date.

In the spec markdown, reference it as:
```markdown
![{Component or screen name}, {date in human-readable format}](assets/YYYY-MM-DD-screenshot.png)
```

If the component or screen contains image fills or icon assets, also use `download_assets` to download each to `02-design/specs/[type]/[component-name]/assets/`. Name files after the Figma layer name, lowercased and hyphenated. Never reference a Figma or CDN URL.

- `index.html`: catalog UI shell. Reads contract, renders live component demos by tier with usage snippets and attribute references. Deployed by `/deploy-catalog`.

## (a) Live production consumers on this branch

There is exactly **one** production entry point. `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/footer/index.tsx` is genuinely live — the base app renders it at `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/_app/index.jsx:484`, resolved to the override by `ccExtensibility` (`package.json:17-20`).

Size `lg` unused. |

**Stories only (not production):** `zimmButton/index.stories.tsx`, `zimmIcon/index.stories.tsx`, `zimmLogo/index.stories.tsx`, `zimmNavItem/index.stories.tsx`, `zimmTextInput/index.stories.tsx`, `zimmInputAction/index.stories.tsx`. ## (b) Other-branch consumers: **none**

| Branch | ui-kits files | References any of the six? |
|---|---|---|
| `develop`, `main` | 0 | **No** — no `ui-kits/` dir; registry has no `Zimm*` rows |
| `feature/SFCC-89_pdp-ui-static-product-information`, `review/SFCC-89` | 3 (`atoms/.gitkeep`, `atoms/zimmPageToolbar/`) | **No.** PDP imports only `ZimmPageToolbar` (`overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:9`) |

Consumed only by its own `ui-kits/registry.tsx` and the dev page `overrides/app/pages/uikits/index.tsx` |
| `backup/pre-develop-sync`, `backup/pre-rebase-SFCC-55` | 12 | Snapshots of this same SFCC-55 work |

Notably, **SFCC-89/91 PDP did not use ZimmButton for add-to-bag** — the most obvious candidate consumer built its own `zimmPageToolbar` instead. ## (c) Upcoming stories that would consume them

`.docs/memory/sprintScope.md` is a **coarse epic-level dependency map with no story detail** (line 3: `*Draft (2026-06-23). To be refined as sprints are confirmed.*`). Relevant lines:

- `:19` — `**Sprint 0 — Foundation (in progress).**`
- `:26-29` — Sprint 1 (29 Jun – 10 Jul): `**Squad A (FED):**` / `- Common UI Components` / `- Homepage & Navigation (Part 1)`
- `:43-44` — Sprint 2: `- PDP (Part 1)` / `- PLP (Part 1)`
- `:56-58` — Sprint 3: `- PDP (Part 2)` / `- PLP (Part 2)` / `- Cart`
- `:61` — Sprint 3 Squad B: `- Search & Recommendations`
- `:70` — Sprint 4: `- Checkout Flow & Delivery`

> **When working in a sprint, do not reference code, components, hooks, or integrations from a later sprint — they do not exist yet.**

`.docs/memory/projectState.md` has no story list. Three lines cut against the justification:

- `:48` — `**Header override** (\`overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx\`): two-row layout, brand logo via \`BrandLogo\` component ..., uppercase nav with \`::after\` hover animation, Account/Saved/Bag text buttons with matching animation` — **the header nav, logo and buttons are already built and do not use ZimmNavItem, ZimmLogo or ZimmButton.** This is the strongest counter to "header nav will need these."
